chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Talhah ibn Zayd from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) from his father - from Ali (peace be upon him) who said: 'A man should make up what he missed with the Imam at the beginning of his prayer.' Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'And we do not say as the foolish say.' It is not permissible for him to return to bowing in any case, and likewise if he raises his head from prostration before the Imam, he should return to his prostration so that his rising from it is with the Imam. (165) 77 That was narrated - Sa'd ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Hammad ibn Uthman and Khalaf ibn Hammad from Rib'i from Abdullah ibn al-Jarud and al-Fudayl ibn Yasar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: We asked him about a man who prayed behind an Imam whom he follows, and he raised his head from prostration before the Imam raised his head from prostration. He said: 'Let him prostrate again, and whoever catches the Imam having raised his head from bowing, let him bow with him and not count that bowing.'
ai.seo_question: What should a worshipper do if they miss a pillar of prayer while following the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the Shia jurisprudence of *muqaddam* (preceding the Imam) by distinguishing between synchronizing the act itself versus synchronizing the transition; if a follower rises from prostration before the Imam, they must return to prostrate again to ensure their rising occurs simultaneously with the Imam, rather than simply counting the missed prostration. The narration explicitly rejects the view of the 'foolish ones' (often identified as the Hanafis or general Sunni jurists) who might allow the missed act to count without re-synchronizing the movement, emphasizing that the congregational bond relies on the shared state of action. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on precise physical coordination in congregational prayer as a manifestation of unity.
